hints.title: Write both curves as y-functions
hints.body: Because p>0 and x=py, the second curve is y=x2p2 with x≥0. The first is y=px.
hints.recap: Both curves lie in the first quadrant.
hints.pitfall: Squaring does not allow the negative-x half of the parabola.

recall.reminder: Preserve the original domain when rearranging a square-root equation.

hints.title: Find the integration limits
hints.body: The equality px=x2p2 gives x=0 or x=p2. For 0<x<p2, the square-root curve is higher.
hints.pitfall: Dividing by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><msqrt><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow></msqrt></mrow></math> too early can hide the origin intersection.
hints.pause: Set up one definite integral for the enclosed area.

recall.reminder: Area between curves is the integral of upper minus lower between crossings.

hints.title: Integrate with the parameter held constant
hints.body: Apply the power rule to the upper-minus-lower expression, treating the positive parameter as constant.
hints.recap: The enclosed area is obtained by evaluating an antiderivative at the two intersections.
hints.pitfall: Keep the parameter factors throughout the integration and simplify powers using its stated positivity.
hints.pause: Find your antiderivative, substitute both limits and simplify the parameter expression.

recall.reminder: The enclosed area is obtained by evaluating an antiderivative at the two intersections.

solution:
The second curve is y=x2p2 for x≥0. The intersections are (0,0) and (p2,p2), obtained from px=x2p2. Between them, px is the upper curve.

The area is ∫0p2(px−x2p2)dx = [2p3x32−x33p2]0p2 = (23)p4−(13)p4=p43.

Answer D: p43.
